title: Work out what actually failed in the raised beds this summer
body: Two of the four beds did nothing and I have been guessing at why. Write down what was in each, when it went in, and how much sun the bed still gets now that the hedge is taller, into [[obsidian:Vegetable bed rotation]] — so next spring's plan starts from records instead of mood.

title: Replace the chain before it eats the cassette
body: The gauge drops past =0.75=, which is the point where a chain on its own stops being the whole repair. Order it this week.

title: Trace the back bedroom draught to its actual source
body: Cold air comes in somewhere along the north wall and I keep treating symptoms — excluder, heavier curtains — without ever finding the gap. Do it properly on a windy evening with a lit incense stick: skirting, window reveal, the old airbrick, the loft hatch above. *Find it first*, then decide what fixing it costs.

title: Learn one braise well enough to cook it without the recipe
body: Same cut, same pot, once a week, until the timings live in my hands rather than on the page.

title: Ten minutes of scales before anything else, every day
body: Fifteen would be better, but ten is the number I will actually keep. What matters here is /consistency/, not volume.

title: Book the timing belt change instead of deferring it again
body: The interval passed some thousands of kilometres ago and this failure mode is not gradual — the belt either holds or it ruins the engine. Get one quote from the independent garage and put a date in the calendar.

title: Commit to one Saturday a month at the river clean-up
body: One morning, entered as a recurring event, so it stops depending on how the week went.

title: Print six photographs rather than add another thousand to the drive
body: Choosing the six is the part that teaches something: it forces a judgement the archive never asks for. Order them as *proper prints* at a decent size, hang four, keep two loose in a folder. Almost everything I still remember about other people's photographs, I saw printed.

title: Teach the heavier games from a player aid, not the rulebook
body: New players drown when setup and win conditions arrive in rulebook order. Write one page per game: what you are trying to do, what you may do on a turn, and the three rules everybody gets wrong the first time. Teach from that sheet and let the rulebook settle arguments.

title: Log garden sightings properly instead of remembering them badly
body:
I can say roughly which birds use the garden and nothing more precise, which means I cannot see a trend at all — whether the greenfinches really stopped coming, or whether I stopped noticing. Fixed rule: one hour, same window, same time on Sunday morning, and record the highest count of each species seen at once. That last convention is the whole point, because it is what keeps the weeks comparable instead of turning into a tally of one bird coming back repeatedly.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citizen_science

title: Get every statement for the year into one folder
body: Four banks, two brokers and a pension provider, none of which deliver anything to the same place. Pull the annual documents into =~/documents/finance/2026/= under one naming scheme, and note which providers only keep them available online for a limited period.

title: Plan the three-day ridge walk around water, not mileage
body: Distance is the easy part to plan and water is what actually decides the day. Mark every reliable source along the route, check which of them are seasonal, and set the two camps from those rather than from tidy daily numbers. Then update [[obsidian:Three-day routes near home]] with the version I would be willing to hand to somebody else.

title: Flatten the bench top before blaming my own joinery
body: The winding sticks say it is twisted, which explains rather more of my bad joints than my technique does.

title: Switch the cats to timed feeding and weigh them weekly
body: Free feeding stopped working the moment there were two of them. Split the daily ration into timed portions, and write a weekly weight in the same notebook as the vet visits — a slow drift is only visible if somebody records it.

title: Find out who the street behind the station is named for
body: It is two minutes from my door and I have never known. The city archive is where to start: the old street directories and the 1890s survey sheets, both consultable without booking ahead, and the name may well turn out to be a landowner rather than anybody worth remembering. Write whatever I find into [[obsidian:Notes on the neighbourhood]], dead ends included, because the dead ends are what stop me running the same search again in two years.
